facts.text: The module path `mcp.server.fastmcp` is removed entirely in v2; everything that lived there moves to `mcp.server.mcpserver`. Any `from mcp.server.fastmcp import X` or `import mcp.server.fastmcp` must become `from mcp.server.mcpserver import X` (respectively the equivalent `mcp.server.mcpserver` module import).

The main server class `FastMCP` is renamed to `MCPServer`. `FastMCP` no longer exists under that name anywhere in the package. Every place that imports it, uses it as a type annotation, subclasses it, or constructs it (`FastMCP(...)`) must change the identifier itself to `MCPServer` — it is a real class rename, not only a change of import location.

The `Context` class moves with the rest of the module: `from mcp.server.fastmcp import Context` → `from mcp.server.mcpserver import Context`. However, `Context` KEEPS its own name — nothing else about `Context` changes (its methods, its behavior, or its use as a type annotation elsewhere). Only the import path is affected.

On the MCP client side, tool metadata objects returned by the SDK change field-naming convention from camelCase to snake_case: `tool.inputSchema` is renamed to `tool.input_schema`. Client code reading `.inputSchema` off a discovered tool object must change.
`ClientSessionGroup.call_tool()` (the class managing calls across a group of client sessions) has a changed calling contract in v2, so such call sites need editing.
Plain `ClientSession.call_tool()` (a single session, as opposed to `ClientSessionGroup`) is UNCHANGED — do not conflate the two classes; single-session `call_tool()` calls must not be flagged.

The SDK's own internal HTTP transport dependency changed from the `httpx` package to `httpx2`. This is purely internal to the SDK's implementation and has zero relevance to application code that imports and uses the separate `httpx` package for its own purposes (e.g. its own unrelated HTTP calls). Ordinary application-level `httpx` usage must NOT be flagged just because the token matches.
CONFIRMED UNCHANGED: the `@mcp.tool()`, `@mcp.resource()`, and `@mcp.prompt()` decorators have identical signature and behavior in v2 — do not flag them.
CONFIRMED UNCHANGED: `.add_tool(...)` is unchanged in v2 — do not flag it.

CONFIRMED UNCHANGED: `ctx.error(...)` / `ctx.info(...)` calls that do NOT pass an `extra=` keyword argument are unchanged and must be treated as unaffected. (Calls that DO pass `extra=` have a different, changed signature.)
CONFIRMED UNCHANGED: `get_context()` is unchanged in v2 — do not flag it.
CONFIRMED UNCHANGED: anything imported from `mcp.types` is unaffected; this subpackage remains aliased and working in v2.
The listed items are the ONLY confirmed changes in this migration; anything not described in the spec is unaffected, including things one might expect to be affected.

Affected sites include ones reached indirectly through a repo's own helper functions and test files, and also string literals that reference the old module path `mcp.server.fastmcp` (e.g. inside test mocks/patch targets), which must be updated to `mcp.server.mcpserver`.
